lessons.title: Story Time: The Rainbow Fish
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss the moral/message of a sea creature story.
success_criteria: I can say what happened in the story.
I can say what the story teaches us.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict the story from sea creature pictures.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a sea-creature story with a moral message (e.g. The Rainbow Fish), discussing its meaning.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record what the story teaches about sharing/kindness.

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the message in full sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of story message — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time you shared something.

lessons.title: Halves and Quarters Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find half and a quarter of shapes and quantities.
success_criteria: I can find half of a shape/quantity.
I can find a quarter of a shape/quantity.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap halves and quarters from Week 5.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding half and quarter of sea-creature themed shapes and quantities.
lessons.independent_task: Children find half/quarter of given sea-creature shapes and quantities.
key_questions: What is a quarter of this?

differentiation.greater_depth: Find half and quarter independently, explaining reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Record fraction understanding progress — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Find half of a group of objects at home.

lessons.title: What Is a Fish?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features common to fish.
success_criteria: I can name a feature of a fish.
I can name a fish.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of different fish.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss common features of fish (gills, fins, scales, live in water).
lessons.independent_task: Children label a fish diagram with key features.
key_questions: What helps a fish breathe underwater?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add extra detail and compare two fish species

lessons.assessment_notes: Note animal feature identification — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Look up a fish species together.

lessons.title: Painting Sea Creatures
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use paint to create a sea creature with texture.
success_criteria: I can paint a sea creature shape.
I can add texture with a technique.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at sea creature pictures for inspiration.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model painting a sea creature and adding texture (e.g. sponge dabbing for scales).
lessons.independent_task: Children paint their own sea creature, experimenting with texture techniques.
key_questions: What texture technique are you using?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe texture technique use — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.home_link: Look for texture patterns in nature at home.

lessons.title: Writing About My Sea Creature
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about a sea creature.
success_criteria: I can describe what my sea creature looks like.
I can write a full sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sea creature paintings from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing descriptive sentences about a sea creature using adjectives.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing their painted sea creature.
key_questions: What does your sea creature look like?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Describe a sea creature to your family.

lessons.title: Counting Sea Creatures to 20
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and record sets of objects to 20.
success_criteria: I can count a set of sea creatures.
I can write the numeral.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting sea-creature counters into sets, recording numerals.
lessons.independent_task: Children count sets of sea-creature counters up to 20, recording numerals.
key_questions: How many sea creatures in this set?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy to 20 — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count a collection of toys or objects at home.

lessons.title: What Is a Mammal? (Dolphins and Whales)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of sea mammals.
success_criteria: I can name a sea mammal.
I can say one way it's different from a fish.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss dolphins and whales — are they fish?
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss that dolphins/whales are mammals that breathe air, unlike fish.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare a fish and a sea mammal, recording one similarity and one difference.
resources_needed: Fish and sea mammal picture cards
key_questions: How is a whale different from a fish?

differentiation.support: Compare with adult support, one difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note classification understanding (fish vs mammal) — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap fish vs sea mammal differences.
lessons.home_link: Look up a fact about dolphins or whales together.

lessons.title: Studying an Artist: Matisse's Sea Creatures
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of an artist's sea-themed work.
success_criteria: I can describe what I notice in the artwork.
I can try a similar technique.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at Matisse's cut-out sea creature artworks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss Matisse's cut-out collage technique and bold use of colour and shape.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own cut-paper sea creature in the style of Matisse.
key_questions: What do you notice about Matisse's work?

differentiation.greater_depth: Combine multiple shapes into a detailed composition

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe understanding and application of an artist's technique — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Look up Matisse's artwork together if possible.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Sea Creature Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read sea-creature-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read sea creature words.
I can read a sentence about the sea.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending sea-creature-themed words (e.g. 'shark', 'crab', 'shell').
lessons.independent_task: Children read sea-creature-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading sea creature words over the week.

lessons.title: Comparing Length: Sea Creature Sizes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and order sea creatures by length.
success_criteria: I can say which sea creature is longer.
I can order 3 sea creatures by length.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing lengths of sea creature pictures/models using non-standard units.
lessons.independent_task: Children order sea creature picture cards from shortest to longest, measuring with cubes.
resources_needed: Sea creature picture cards of varying sizes
key_questions: How many cubes long is it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record length comparison and ordering skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare the length of two toys at home.

lessons.title: Camouflage and Colour in the Sea
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why some sea creatures use camouflage.
success_criteria: I can say what camouflage is.
I can name a sea creature that uses it.
lessons.starter_activity: Play a hidden picture game to introduce camouflage.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss camouflage in sea creatures (e.g. flatfish, octopus) and why it helps them survive.
lessons.independent_task: Children design a camouflaged sea creature for a chosen background, explaining their choices.
key_questions: Why does this creature need camouflage?
How does your design blend in?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain camouflage's survival benefit in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of adaptation for survival — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Look for camouflage examples in animals at home or in books.

lessons.title: Sea Creature Sculpture with Salt Dough
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to shape a 3D sea creature using salt dough.
success_criteria: I can shape a sea creature form.
I can add texture/detail.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model shaping a simple sea creature form using pinching and rolling techniques.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a 3D sea creature sculpture using salt dough, adding texture with tools.
key_questions: What sea creature are you making?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add fine detail and combine multiple shapes

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe 3D shaping and fine motor control — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.home_link: Make a model with playdough or plasticine at home.

lessons.title: Sea Creature Riddles
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a sea creature clearly enough for others to guess it.
success_criteria: I can give 3 clues about my sea creature.
I can guess a friend's sea creature.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models a riddle about a sea creature.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how to give clear clues without naming the creature.
lessons.independent_task: Children create and share sea creature riddles in pairs, guessing each other's.
resources_needed: Sea creature picture cards for reference
key_questions: Can you guess my sea creature?

differentiation.support: Use picture cards to prompt clues

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive spoken language skill — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Share favourite riddles with the class.
lessons.home_link: Make up a sea creature riddle for your family.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction: Sea Creature Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve mixed word problems using a sea creature context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving mixed word problems using a sea creature context (e.g. fish joining/leaving a shoal).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve sea-creature-themed word problems, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a sea creature word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Ocean Food Chains (Simple Introduction)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a simple ocean 'who eats who' relationship.
success_criteria: I can say what one sea creature eats.
I can order a simple 'eats' chain.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce a very simple food chain concept (e.g. small fish eaten by big fish eaten by shark).
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence a simple 3-step ocean food chain using picture cards.
key_questions: What comes next in the chain?

differentiation.greater_depth: Sequence a 4+ step chain and explain each link

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of feeding relationships — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what different animals eat at home.

lessons.title: Under the Sea Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about sea creatures.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's sea creature learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about sea creatures, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on sea creatures you learned about.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Fractions, Length
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, fraction, and length skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can count to 20.
I can find half/quarter.
I can compare length.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of counting, fractions and length comparison.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: counting, fractions, length comparison.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 19 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N4/MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising fractions and length over the weekend.

lessons.title: Under the Sea Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about sea creatures learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name 3 sea creatures.
I can describe one adaptation (camouflage, gills, breathing air).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering fish, mammals, camouflage, and food chains.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Under the Sea' display.
key_questions: What sea creature did you learn about?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note animal classification and adaptation understanding — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's under the sea learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about sea creatures with your family.

lessons.title: Under the Sea Class Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to contribute art pieces to a collaborative under-the-sea scene.
success_criteria: I can add my art piece to the display.
I can talk about my contribution.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all art created this week (paintings, cut-outs, sculptures).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss arranging individual pieces into a collaborative under-the-sea scene display.
lessons.independent_task: Children help arrange their sea creature art into a large collaborative under-the-sea display.
key_questions: Where should your creature go in the scene?
What does your creature add to the display?

differentiation.greater_depth: Suggest arrangement ideas for the whole display

lessons.assessment_notes: Note collaborative and reflective art skills across the topic — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class admiration of the finished under-the-sea display.
lessons.home_link: Describe the class under-the-sea display to your family.
